A Short Field Report: (Central Powers defending the sector in Aisne)
...I was deployed in a squad of 4 and was delivered an old 1880 Komission Gewehr... Our squad was ordered to hold the right side of our trench. The Belgians have already started their assault on our positions by first crossing a road and then advancing over an open field. As I jumped into a crater to set up my defensive position a young Belgian soldier bumped right into me... First, I was so scared...How the hell did he manage to reach our lines already???
Without too much thinking, I fired my rifle.. The bullet hit him in the neck and he started to bleed heavily... He fell on the ground while grabbing his neck with both hands in agony in order to prevent the blood to drain from his wound...He was screaming in fear... His voices... I was just standing beside him and couldnt do a thing..."What have I done!?"... His voices started fading away... I knew in my head that I have to pull myself together and return to my duty...so I left him rott there in that crater...I decided to move up to look over the edge of the crater to see how the assault was nearing to an end...I turned to the left and saw one of the Landsers deploying his MG on a sandbag while a whole squad of Belgians was advancing on him... He managed to reload his gun in time and opened fire on them...The bullets whizzled through the air and penetrated the skin  and bones of the advancing soldiers...It all happened in a matter of seconds...They were massacred..in an open field with no cover at all..but thats how this Great War was like...

Can't remember when or how i found out about this game but i am so happy i did! The maps (for me) do an incedible job of creating and conveying that "feel" of a heavily bombed and trenched landscape. [[EDIT]] I have been having a bit of a problem at the end of battle which sometimes results in the game hanging in such a way that i have to (manually via alt-tab) close it down and re-start the client/game. Again annoying, but not game breaking for me as it seems to only happen once every 5 or 6 matches. [edit] Two days and an update later the issue is completly resolved. If by some miracle the devs read this you guys rock!
Also the graphics are beautiful all around with some nice animations for a beta too. Although the movement and associated animations can feel a bit sloppy (reminds me a bit of arma 2) it's a good starting point. Sounds are great as well. Again it's a beta, but probably the most stable and playable beta i've ever had the pleasure of being a part of. Just in case it matters to you, I run Verdun with everything turned UP as high as it goes!
[My PC = i7 4770 + GTX 770 4GB oc]
Here (as in the real trenches of WW1) if you are silly enough to poke your head up to take a look over the trench, you will most likley catch a bullet in the face. So team work, timing and caution are key. Also the fact that every one is packing a single shot bolt action rifle means that running blindly around a corner, or skylining a ridge or hill top will result in you getting shot (again) and possibly giving your squads position away. I also love the way the battle flows in a similar way to the battles of the first war. Men were massed, a whistle was blown and they went over the top to take the enemy position. The gameplay is a similar series of attacks and counter atacks with little to no ground changing hands (just like the real deal).
Many will not like this as a shooter for many different reasons and thats ok. But if you're looking for something a little harder than the usual shooter Verdun offes what i feel is a refreshing take on the trenches of the first world war. This game requires a more thought out and "calm under fire" aproach. Move as a group, don't bunch up, cover your corners and listen for the gunfire. I can't wait to see what the developers (who are very active and open to feedback) add to the game next!
22/07/14 - Still loving this game. Animations and sounds have been improved and some time soon (I hope) they will be adding gas attacks. This should really shake things up in terms of game play and make storming that trench all the more deadly!
15/02/15 - It just keeps getting better! Now with a new engine this game is starting to really take shape. The graphics are better, the physics (bullet drop/lead) are good and getting better. Gas attacks, trench clubs and to top it all off they now have an Australia/Pacific server. Constant updates and feedback from both the community and the devs keep this game evolving and moving in a very positive direction.

What do i think of Verdun?
I think ti's a really good concept that they tried to grasp and make into a video game, you don't see many fps games during WWl or before so to see this out on the market really caught my attention by itself.
I'll start by saying i got this game early december and there was a update or two but that was it, i began to think the devs just took my money and ran away. However recently they just had a update and i've gotta say they've improved the game a lot and it looks a lot nicer too.
The game is unique in its own way because the fighting style is just like WWl and if you don't know what  i mean well then it's all pretty much trench warfare so close combat kinda stuff and it's a attack/defend style. So one side, ex. the germans, will leave their own trench and run across no mans land. No mans land is pretty self explanitory it's called that because no one wants to be there. It's covered in barbed wire (which if you run in will slow you down and kill you) and is just an open field, the only cover you can use to help yourself are the shell holes that are scatered around. While all this is going on the french are sitting in their trench with their rifles/mgs just mowing you guys down, and you're just praying that you'll somehow sneak into their trench and capture it.
The game trys to make teamplay an important thing by giving you extra points if you work as a squad. There are 4 different roles in each squad that are all unique in their own ways.
You have a NCO that carries a pistol and commands orders of where to attack or can place motor fire down on a position
There's the classic rifleman you obviously has a rifle, pretty basic
You can be the Support role which carrys an old WWl mg (which is♥♥♥♥♥♥btw) and covers your teammates as they move up or you can be that badass mowing down the enemy as they advance forward
Lastly there's the sniper which is pretty self explanitory
The game is also somewhat active, you can find games to play in and have fun and even every now and again join a full game.
The downsides.
Even though you can find games like i just said it's also a down side because there are usually only 3, 4 at the most you can join.
The lag can be pretty bad at times and you can't vote kick people out of games. For example i was playing last night and a guy on my squad had a ping of +650. He was making the whole game lag up and there was nothing we could do and he wouldn't leave so therefor i had to leave.
They only have two gamemodes to play, The classic attack/defend and the other is free for all.
Free for all is a lot of fun....IF you can get a game going. There's usually only about 2-4 people playing free for all so you're never getting the full expierence that they wanted you have with the gamemode. so you're always stuck then playing attack/defend
The other thing that's bad about this game is it's community. The people you play with are either a complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to you or don't know what the ♥♥♥♥ they're doing and while they should b rushing and attacking they are camping in the back with rifles sniping so you never advance and you lose every match. Every time i've told my team to push up or ask them why they aren't helping me they all tell me to stop complaining.
Over all i give this game a solid 7/10
I think the price may be a tad bit overpriced, i'm not saying they are ripping you off, but if this game goes on sale you should pick up a copy of it for sure.

*April 13, 2014 Early Access Review* (Review will be updated when Verdun is off its beta)
Verdun can be explained in one sentence. A World War I first person team-cooperative shooter with some similarities with Red Orchestra franchise in a sheer blend of fast-pace pitch battles and gunfights. Initially, I really like this game mainly because of its setting and reliance of using instincts in order to survive (like Red Orchestra). However, as I play more, the game seems a bit more like a World War I version of Call of Duty. The previous sentence sounds harsh, but it's not as bad as it sounds. While the game seems to tackle in a semi-realistic gameplay that relies on teamwork, it is unfortunate that the majority of players in the game only cares about K:D ratio and selfish ambitions. Players do not use their roles properly and the only way to win is kill the enemy players as quickly as possible in order to take enemy positions before the enemy spawns. The texture is "alright" and the human faces need significant improvements in terms of facial structure. So far, the community for Verdun is fairly tiny/small but the majority of players are pre-teenagers and immature players who are arrogant that may or may not lead to your team's downfall. What I dislike about Verdun the most is there is little or no teamwork, and that needs to be addressed. Strangely enough, I continue to come back and play the game mainly it has the potential to become a great World War I shooter that can be compared to World War II's Red Orchestra franchise. The game will be good if there are no arrogant players with the attitude that you see in Call of Duty and stronger emphasis on teamwork. The game has my recommendation only because of its potential to become a great game...but by a short margin due to the immaturity of the community.

How would I summarise my experience with Verdun?
In one word: Enjoyable
The game is not your average run of the mill first person shooters which is refreshing to say the least. First difference, of course being the setting of the First World War, which I at least feel like the Wild West genre, has been lacking in the market of first person shooters as both genres prefer to be set more in a strategy game shell. Of course with the release of battlefield 1 this year the WW1 Shooter Genre will have a grand total of three games to memory (WW1 Source being the third). However, I digress. The setting of verdun is interesting and is not too overplayed like modern war shooters to name a setting so oversaturated that the main two competitors have collided and sped off in different directions time period wise.
Another difference between Verdun and the average shooter is the combat scenarios the game places you into. This is World War one so, of course, combat takes place in trench systems and objectives in the standard mode are capturing said trenches whilst killing the opposing side. The game is based more upon marksmanship than speed of combat as both sides are for the most part evenly matched with bolt-action rifles, pistols and the odd light-machine-gun and must defend and attack in succession in order to attain a victory. The game also offers incentives for working as a squad of four (commander, grenadier, sniper and machine-gunner), which around 5-6 make up the average team. Myself at the very least like the idea of this type of battle which is a welcome difference to the lone-wolf run and gun attitude of Call of Duty.
However, my only issue is the leveling, as whilst leveling as a whole is fine in games overall, in Verdun many of the high level players are often the best and many of the games I have played are for the most part with very few in my skill level and so normally the higher ranked players win the majority of games or end in draws.
However, overall I would recommend this game as I personally have had a lot of fun with it.

I feel as if this game could do with having a variety of different game modes rather than Rifle Deathmatch (which sorta gets boring, to be honest) or squads (which seem pointless to incorporate unless you have an objective for the game). There's never anyone playing when I'm playing either, so perhaps some advertisement should be in order. 6/10

To stand out amidst a sea of generic shooters takes a bit of work. Fortunately, Verdun stands out by virtue of the setting - World War I. Despite being almost ideal for translation into gaming, Verdun is the first FPS to really put a player in first-person WWI combat. The attack/defend system is ideal for the core gameplay, and the different abilities within a squad is a nice take on a familiar mechanic. The small dev team is evident as soon you start the game, but really the appeal of Verdun is that it takes place in an oft-overlooked period of history. By that fact, the sort of player that is attracted to this game is also the sort of player who can look past a lack of polish and just enjoy what is a very rare, and very fun gaming experience. I have had this game since October of 2013, and let me tell you right off the bat: this game has improved beyond anything i ever imagined! The graphics, the gameplay, the adjustments, everything! All of these things combined have made it one of the most enjoyable World War One First Person Shooter games i have ever played.
It is a new genre, in my opinion: you cannot use conventional tactics from games such as Red Orchestra, Call of Duty, or even any of the Battlefield games! So be advised that when you first enter the game, it may be frustrating simply because you need to apply new tactics in order to be successful in this World War 1 environment.
This brings me to my second point: do not get frustrated! Instead, look for dangers before they hit...mostly artillery. You can look to the skies and see the streaks of the shots coming down, and you can determine where they will land. If you don't have time to do this, just listen for the distinguishable sounds as they are shot from the artillery pieces off map. Also, do not poke your head out of the trench for too long: you WILL be shot. This, i have come to find, is what frustrates people the most, and it is simply because they have not adjusted to the type of warfare that Verdun, as a game, offers.
Each step is a new obstactle in this game (quite literally!) You may find yourself caught behind an extensive barbed wire fence that you need to get around, or you may be caught of guard and fall into ankle wire only to be picked off by a sniper. Machine guns are deadly in this game as they were in real life: so make sure you are always watching for their flashes so you can get rid of them! Probably two of the most feared obstactles in this game are grenades and artillery. Use them to your benefit, and learn to fear them when they are being wielded by the enemy!
If you follow all of these steps, you will be able to take some time to look at the beauty of the game. They have added in such little details such as dugouts in the sides of trench walls where you can see beds, to little things scattered around the trenches (pots, pans, ammo, boxes, ect.) One of the most beautiful things to watch is an assault. Of course it is not delightful in real life, but being that this IS a game, you will find some epicness in sitting back and watching people run head first to their death.
All and all, i must say that i fell in love with this game at first glance: and i really did just glance at it! It didn't look very promising, but i promise you that these developers, even though they are a small team, know how to make a fun, exciting, and interactive game! I cannot express how much i have enjoyed Verdun: even through all of the hurtles which have made the game frustrating. It is truly a gem, and seeing now the road map for 2015 has gotten me even more excited for what is yet to be implemented into the game!
I definitely recommend this game to any tactical FPS enthusiast, History geek, and people looking for a fun exhilerating ride!

**updated review**
**posted 2014**
As an early access game with a relatively small server population and only 3 developers, Verdun continues to impress me. Verdun being one of a handful of playable First World War games in existence, I was eager to fork out the $15 for the Steam beta. That was around the time the Picardie update was implemented, and I was happy to find that Verdun ran just fine on my laptop. After putting 50 hours into the three maps and finding my niche in the squad system, I can say that Verdun is only getting better.
Verdun offers unique challenges and experiences that cannot be found elsewhere as a relatively simple FPS game. Currently, weapons are historically limited to bolt-action rifles, clunky machine guns, pistols, and grenades. The simplicity in weaponry helps level the playing field and keeps any one player from dominating the other team. Often when storming a trench I will cut down the first man in front of me and the man behind him will take me down while I re-chamber only to be shot by my squad mate that has (hopefully) followed behind. This unique nature of Verdun helps make it playable to most people even if they are bad at a traditional FPS, and I appreciate that.
There are still things that frustrate me about Verdun. Things like prone blocking that keep me from taking cover when it is vital, inactive players blocking the trench, the multiple shots sometimes required to kill, and the inexplicable tendency for small pieces of wood on the map to get in-between my crosshairs and the enemy. I am sure any real problems will be addressed by developers because they are undoubtedly in tune with the dedicated community of players and any useful feedback given to them.
To summarize, Verdun was worth my money and the positive trend of developer support and effort is showing no signs of lessening.
**updated content, 2016**
After a few years of playing Verdun on-and-off since my original purchase, I still recommend this game to any prospective buyer. My previous statement about the positive trend of development has definitely played out over these years. Content including 5 new maps, 8 new squads (with 4 new nationalities represented), nearly 50 new weapons, two new game modes, and an intense gore option have been added (for free) since I first reviewed this game. Lately, new content has been more rare mostly because the developers have been focusing on porting Verdun to the Xbox One (its already out for PS4). After this I'm not sure what will be added but I'm excited to see what it is.
My old complaints are now outdated. Proneblocking does not bother me as much as it used to, whether that's because I got used to it or because they fixed it I'm not sure. The same goes for the multipule shot kills. I think sometime in the past few years the hit system was reworked so all rifles (plus the machinengewehr) are 1-shot kills while pistols/other LMGs are 1-to-2 shot kills. The whole thing about small peices of wood was just the past me being silly.
New players will most likely experience a learning curve. Be sure to read the official steam guides on the weaponry and squad role/leveling system. Also, be aware that most people play the Frontlines gamemode (a trench-by-trench attack/defend match) and that the other three gamemodes are often mostly depopulated. Two things a new player should try to remember is that teamwork is not absolutely necessary but is always preferable, and that having a negative k/d is totally fine because you can still have a great match with 30+ deaths. Many people complain about aim-bots and cheaters, but usually these are just cases of very experienced players laying waste to less experienced/less patient players. If you get frustrated just switch lobbies, or, better yet, join their team.
Finally, after playing this game for over 2 years, I've developed a deep respect for the tone of the game and how the developers have chosen to portray a "generic" soldier's experience of the Western Front during the First World War. Verdun avoids the dramatism and theatrics of most war films and other games like Battlefield 1 and Valiant Hearts (although I would still recommend the latter game). There is no attempt to personalize the player's experience by telling a story or by forcing the player to use charcters with detailed biographies. There are no emotional cutscenes or any dramatic music.
This does not mean that Verdun feels impersonal or inauthentic. Verdun manages to respect the terrible reality that was the First World War by including details which are somewhat unnecessary to the gameplay (like the sheer choice of weapons and the level of uniform detail), heavy but realistic gore mechanics (lots of screaming and loss of limbs), and refusing to center the experience of the game around a handful of fictional individuals. I feel that Verdun's lack of storytelling and non-linear multiplayer allows my experience of the game to be more organic, and, as a result, it feels more authentic and "real."
To summarize again, Verdun was totally worth my money and the game itself is set apart for its high level of histroically accurate detail as well as its dedicated and responsive developers. If its on sale and you are on the fence, go for it! It is much cheaper than BF 1 after all....

Verdun is an FPS game that brings back the more realistic and strategic gun game. Unlike 99% of FPS games made, only 1 or 2 shots will kill an enemy and you can really feel the burden of your equipment. Players must try to run gaps, crouch behind cover, and lay prone in ditches in order to stay hidden. Its atmosphere is well made and really enhance the gameplay. So far there are only 2 modes, deathmatch, and frontline.
Deathmatch is like it sounds, you choose a gun, and fight everyone you see and try not to die (much). Frontlines is a very nice system that matches with the war theme. It is a mixture of capture the flag and deathmatch. Much like battlefield, there are 2 teams and in each team a number of squads. But in each squad there are only 4 classes and each one can only be chosen once. This makes it so communication and strategy is a must in order to do well for the team. The goal is to attack the trenches or defend them. Kind of like tug of war, each side must try to overcome the enemy and gain the most territory.
Overall, I am having a very good time playing this game and recommend it to those looking for a good fps game that is not a bullet sponge fest. Yes, there are many bugs and it is not optimized very well yet, but it is also early access and those things will be fixed over time. The content that is in the game right now is well done and once it gains more content and a larger following, it will be a long lasting game that will provide many hours of fun.

text: Verdun is one of the most emotionally overwhelming games I have ever come across, and it accomplishes this without a backstory or voice acting. There is no single player campaign to ignore over multiplayer, no characters to love and hate. Many milllitary games attempt to replicate dramatic news reel footage during gameplay cut scenes, Verdun does not. But it does present an experience from a soldiers perspective, not with poorly written dialog and overly dramatic voice acting, but through the emotions invoked in the player during gameplay. I play this game thinking of a great-uncle, who I never met, but know through family stories. Seeing The opposing team storm a trench I am hiding in (while I am armed only with a bolt action rifle)  is an incredibly terrifing experience that I can only imagine he experienced many times during his service. I'm sure that my experience is entirly unique to me in its emotional power. And that it's all a product of an overactive imagination, but I like that Verdun allows me to make the game fit my story. I haven't played a game since my childhood which has made me want to be so imaginative while I play. Verdun has issues most triple A titles wish they had during Beta and even some launch titles (BF3, and anyother EA title in the last 7 years). Remember, this is what Beta meant 10 years ago. As in, this is an actual Beta and not a prerelease copy of a finished game.

Verdun takes us back 100 years ago, durning "The Great War'". Personally I'm glad to finally see this period of our beautiful history taken onto digital entertainment.
At first you may think it's one of those Red Orchestra title, with unsteady recoil and other "realistic" implements, however the answer is no. Verdun aims to be in the middle between "realistic" let's say Red Orchestra style and bit casual Call of Duty 2( no bullet drop and etc)  and it does it very well. Therfore both groups of players should find Verdun suitable for them. Yes, we have seen it with RO 2 where the devs tried to make the game more "easy" to attrack casual players and we all know how that ended. Verdun is different.
The key of the game are so called squads, now before you start playing you might want to read very well written guide about it, trust me it will save you being confused when you start playing the game. In other games for example Battlefield the squad thing is optional with Verdun it's a must do thing, you can't pass it. Squads in Verdun make gameplay both tactical and dynamic, if you already have some friends to work together the gameplay expierience will be really pleasant. If not then I'm sure after a while you'll find some friends that will play with you.
One of the things that I really liked about the game is the "Counter attack" mode, where you take the objective and then have to hold it and vice versa if you lose it, just like in WWI, huh.
The devs are constantly working to offer us more and better therfore the future of the game looks promising.
If you are into "WWII" shooters definitely give it a go, no matter if you are into realistic or casual shooters. Verdun offers fun and "epic" gameplay for both.

Counter-Strike: Source reprises the player back into the Counter-Strike universe by utilizing the Source Engine, the successor to GoldSrc on which the original award-winning Counter-Strike and Counter-Strike: Condition Zero ran on. Many aspects and mechanics have stayed in CS: S, which involve more teamwork and strategy coupled with timing and steadying your shots to truly play the game. You play as Terrorists, who either hold hostages, plant bombs in bombsites, and/or eliminate the opposing team, Counter-Terrorists. As a Counter-Terrorist, your job is to either save the hostages, defuse planted bombs, and/or eliminate the Terrorists.
There are also many mods out there from various sites like Game Banana to expand your CS: S experience. Whether from model re-skins to custom community-made maps, the experience never ends thanks to the Source Engine.
If you own a legit copy of Garry's Mod, CS: S is a must for the majority of assets available in GMod require CS: S, although there is low-res fallback assets in case you don't have CS:S. Either way, CS: S is a must for a FPS player looking for teamwork and strategy within a quick playfield.

This game is a perfect example of why we need more World War 1 games. A setting like this is perfect for frontline, territorial combat, and despite the game still being in beta it pulls this off really well. A match consists of two phases, the defense, and the attack, repeated back and forth until one side pushes the other all the way back to their last line of defense. Much like actual battles in the Great War, if you're familiar with highschool level History, you go 'over the top' and leave the safety of your trench, and storm into the barbed wire and crater ridden field ahead and assault the enemy's front line. From fighting trench to trench to clearing them out, this game is incredibly entertaining. To give an idea, it feels a lot like Red Orchestra but in World War 1.
Just keep in mind that this game is not fully released, and the graphics and animations don't seem quite too polished just yet. This is addressed by the devs whenever you start the game anyway, and they claim they are continuing to work hard on polishing the game. But don't let that make you hesitant on buying, it's a super fun game regardless and will only get better from here on out.

Now, this is still in beta and if people voice these issues they will most likely get solved, the community is pretty close-knit, and trench warfare is a brand new take on the FPS genre, and with a little refinement and instruction, can be really fun. Definitely support the developers by buying this game if you like it, happy shooting!

Counter-Strike 1.6 got me into shooters and PC-games in general, Source bound me to them. There's no rewards to be gained in the form of skins, perks or leveling up and that's what makes it so attractive both casually and competitively. Yes, there's a good chance you'll play with people who've played for years. But they don't have an equipment or upgrade advantage because of it. Everyone starts the match with the same amount of cash and same weapon so getting more money and an early weapon advantage all depends on how well you perform. And if you're a FPS player in general then you're probably on equal footing skill-wise as well.
This game has proven itself year after year after freaking year, even with its also great successor being out for a while now.

This game, as it stands, still has a way to go.
As-is Verdun is a playable, somewhat enjoyable, WWI shooter. For the vast majority of players I suspect the meat-grinder gameplay may be a turn off, however.
The maps are spacious and open, providing plenty of long distance shot opportunities for riflemen, which rule the day in the game right now. Your machine gunners and NCOs add some variety but the classes with the powerful bolt action rifles do most of the damage. Machine guns must be deployed and taken down, which gives the riflemen plenty of time to line up a shot and take them down. This is realistic and not necessarily a complaint but it does tend to limit the usefulness of your MG classes.
Matches involve a lot of keeping your head down and waiting for targets to peek out from cover. You may occasionally push up and take an objective but it is a slow push, the defenders have all the advantages which is in line with the trench-war setting. Go into Verdun expecting a somewhat sloggy, mostly realistic shooter.
Assuming you aren't a twitch gamer and don't get frustrated with repeated deaths you can have a lot of fun with this game. There are glitches here and there, your character models tend to hang up on things from time to time, and barbed wire is the deadliest substance known to man in this game but as long as you take it all with a grain of salt there is plenty of enjoyment to be squeezed out of Verdun right now. Here's to hoping the game only gets better.

Counter Strike: Source
If you want an honest and accurate review of this game, instead of over-hyped and fallacious fanboy critiques, read on.
+ A lot of different firearms to use, such as pistols, shotguns, submachineguns and sniper rifles..great variety.
+ Plenty of multiplayer maps to indulge in with a massive community still playing.
+ Singleplayer mode versus bots, which is fun for anyone and ideal for a relaxing playthrough. I really enjoyed this.
- Overly simplistic and primitive shooting. Iron sight zooming on all weapons is non-existent and only sniper rifles allow a scope zoom. The game relies heavily on crosshairs, which is an outdated idea. Counter Strike: Source was released in 2004, but has never been adjusted with time by developers, so it remains backward.
- This game's multiplayer is not in any way tactical. It is focused on camping, 'bunny-hopping' to avoid bullets and flashbang grenade spamming. This is not skillfull or realistic.
- The game is not team oriented, despite the very obvious fact you have players on your multiplayer side. Other than that, the teams do not work together or use microphone frequently for communication, so any chances of formulating an assault strategy or defence is utterly futile.
- Poor graphics which haven't been updated since 2004 and it seems, never will be.
- No storyline mode to the game, meaning it is a purely multiplayer or singleplayer versus bots experience. There's no background or explanation for why the counter-terrorists are fighting terrorists, I can only surmise it's because that's their job, but it leaves me dissatisfied.
Overall Score: 5/10
Counter: Strike Source is a terrible multiplayer game. But, it is a really good singleplayer versus bots game which I had fun with. The multiplayer pulls the score down significantly. You can easily spend over 100 hours replaying maps against bots and enjoying yourself. If you're looking for a good multiplayer First Person Shooter, it's probably a better idea to check out Counter: Strike Global offensive, a far more modernised game than this one, albeit I suspect it will suffer from similar shortcomings.

Verdun is supposedly the first WWI FPS. Made by two indie companies with a total of three developers, while many think such low development wouldn't be successful, the game proves them wrong.
Graphics in this game are superb, not many people expect much more out of an indie company. There are some graphic options in the menu however I wish there was just a bit more. Currently there are no sound controls, but the developers said they will add it in at a later date. As far as the battlefields go, they are rather spectacular, however somewhat bland. There is detail in every little part, with huge craters in no man's land, dead animals in the middle of no man's land barbed wire all over, it gives the player a feeling like they are actually experiencing WWI. Currently there are three maps, but I believe that they are working on adding more, all three look authentic and believable. However there are some drawbacks. Low frame rates haunt almost every player in this beta, while not unplayable it's more annoying, especially when you get killed because your fps dropped during the action. Hopefully this can be fixed before release. (UPDATE: Devs have released an update, upgrading their engine and fixing some lag, while I still experience some, it is minimized.)  The menus are a bit buggy, but overall the devs have done a superb job on the visual side.
Gameplay is supposedly centered around you squad and your role in it. Yet with no current voice chat and little incentive to stay with your squad, your officer could be on the complete other side of the map and it would have no influence on your gameplay. However if you play with your friends and you really drive your squad based gameplay, it can actually help, turning your squad into a cruel fighting machine. This game has a leveling up system, your squad levels up with new uniforms and tech, and you have your own level, aswell as your rifles get leveled up. The leveling system needs some work as it doesn't seem like it is that responsive or effective. The main mode (or atleast what I presume is the main mode) is what their version of what the western front is. You get a set amount of time to storm the enemy trench with your team. If you can kill everyone in that trench and hold it for a set amount of time that is now your front line trench and you have to defend for the same amount of time. However if you are unsuccessful in storming the trench, you have about 30 seconds to retreat back into your trench and defend. If you don't make it back in 30 seconds you're deemed a deserter and are killed, but more on that later. I assume the gameplay is actually decently realistic, removing some factors, but is pretty fun. The other game mode is a rifle deathmatch. Basically it is a free for fall across the entire map. This is a great way to work out the maps and practice your rifling skills. One of the problems with this game is that you die way too much. It's easy to die in a normal game 30+ times. Some would call this being realistic and I get that, but at points it can just be annoying. Another aspect mentioned earlier is that if you go outside the area of the map the game wants you to be in you can be killed because you're "abandoning". If you go behind where you're supposed to, you are killed. If you leave you're trench and go forward when defending you are killed. If you're attacking and you go past their trench you are killed. This can get annoying, however it does push the WWI playstyle so it is not such a madhouse. Another annoying feature is how deadly the barbed wire is. One can simply run into them and die a few seconds later, I don't know how realistic this is, but it sure is annoying if you don't see it. The gameplay is fun, although I hope they optimize it more to make it a great game.
This game is currently solely multiplayer, however the devs had mentioned in the forums they are looking to add a multiplayer mode with bots, which I really hope they do, just incase I can't play online. As far as online goes the players are actually extremely nice. The players on this game are no Dota players, they actually help you out, even if they are on the opposite team, and I've seen that the teams have joked around with each other creating a great environment. Most everyone in the forums are nice aswell, answering my questions and inviting me to play with them when I didn't even ask. I hope that this can remain true beyond it's release.
The devs are working on many things, they just released a nice Christmas update where there is a new Christmas map and you can throw snowballs at one another. This is a nice little addition, and unneeded, but it was nice of them to add it. The devs say that they will add more before release and I hope they can come through, The game is really spectacular for just three devs, and I look forward to more.
Verdun is a unique WWI first person shooter by a dedicated indie team that pulled it off with a great dynamic gameplay and different game modes. With a few minor drawbacks this is a great experience any first person shooter or history fanatic should checkout, and I know I'll be playing for awhile..

Having played Red Orchestra since the mod days and having played this since before it was Greenlit, I think I can speak with some modicum of authority:
They feel similar, but only insofar in that you are armed with a bolt-action rifle. The combat is much more fluid in Red Orchestra, with houses being stormed and counter-stormed multiple times in a small handful of minutes.
Verdun revolves entirely around the mechanic of "one team attacks, the other defends" When a timer hits zero, the other team attacks and the other defends, if a team should take the objective, they are immediately on the defensive and the other team can take back the objective.
That being said, the game isn't just a huge "let's sit around and snipe at each other" simulator, when a team has to attack, you see organized efforts on the part of the 4-man squads as they attempt to cross no-man's-land and storm the enemy trenches. Once in the trenches, the combat becomes very frantic and brutal. Hell, the last server I was on, I got 7 kills with my bayonet while repelling enemy assaults. When Verdun is at range, it acts much more naturally than Red Orchestra. When Verdun is up close, it still acts more naturally, despite the wonky melee controls (at the moment).
Red Orchestra captures that feeling of urban brawl that made up so much of the Eastern Front (cos let's face it, most of the non-urban maps in RO2 blow due to the lack of tanks), Verdun captures that feeling of "attack and defend" that the Western Front was made up of.
At the moment, Verdun doesn't have trench guns or spiked clubs or bundles upon bundles of grenades, but they're coming. Gas attacks are planned for January (apparently), which will make the already hazy battlefield an absolute mess until the enemy is right on top of you. I highly recommend getting Verdun if you like Red Orchestra. I highly recommend getting Verdun if you liked Call of Duty 1 and 2 rifles only. I highly recommend Verdun if you want something new to experience and play.

Verdun is a game which is an early access beta game, but even so it is already spectacular!  It is different from most first person shooters in that it is highly cooperative on each of the sides.  Individuals must join a squad which is comprised of four people each of which have different roles within the squad.  If success is to be had, it comes as being a member of a squad, and not just one of many soloists as is commonplace in most other first person shooters.  This not only gives it a unique flavor, but also gives it a strong feeling of what it was like to be fighting in World War One.  To my knowledge, this is the only World War One first person shooter ever to exist.  Other than a few flight simulators, there have been practically no games on the subject of World War One at all.
My Grandfather was a veteran of the "Great War" which is what it was called up until the conclusion of World War Two.  He was an officer in a tank battalion and commanded a young tanker who would eventually become famous as a World War Two hero, tanker, and general: George Patton.
I highly recommend this game.  The authors are continuously updating it, sometimes as frequently as several times a day, but never less than a couple times a week.  They are dedicated to creating a great game, and thus far they have succeeded fantastically.  This game is worth every penny even in this stage of beta, and I'm sure that when it reaches its final release version, it will rank up there with the best first person shooters of all time.  Count yourself lucky by shelling out some cash, and becoming an early release beta tester of this wonderful new game.  I assure you, you will not be sorry.

- Developer communication with community could be better (It can be weeks before the devs will talk about what they are working on, updates, patches, etc.)
- Rifle deathmatch has not been supported for a while now, so why keep it in the game?
- Verdun runs on the Unity engine, need I say more?
Conclusion:
If you're looking for a unique multiplayer FPS that has potential, Verdun may be for you.  l recommend Verdun but with a caveat: Verdun has been in Early Access for two years now, so adjust your expectations accordingly.

Firstly, I love this game because you can drive all over Europe. You have to manage your money, and make sure that, when you get out a loan from the bank, you have enough money to pay it back, or are at least making enough daily profit to pay it back.
You also manage a business. You can hire drivers to work for you, and they will complete jobs for you, but you have to pay them a wage, plus some for every journey they complete. You level up they skills, that make them be better at certian things, like you can make them earn more money for going over a set distance, or you can make them carry high value or fragile cargo. They can also carry ADR materials, so things that could be dangourous. But you get paid more for that.
You can always do 'Quick Jobs', and these are when the employer provides the truck, and you just go where they tell you. This is fun, but it starts to get boring, only doing short deliverys, so you can buy a truck, so that you can go further distances, and get more money.
To conclude, I feel that anybody who likes games like Farm Simulator, or any simulator game should give this game a try, because it is a great way to unwind after a long day, and I have found it to be so much fun and very calming. Some people say that this is a boring game, I happen to disagree.

This game is hands down amazing. Many of the people that play CSS are veterans and have a lot of skill and experience with the  game. There are no overpowered guns, however some guns are better than others on certain maps. Since the people that play CSS are veterans, they are usually good and provide a challenge for new players such as me. The game seems to run best on teamwork because it is almost impossible to win if your team is not helping each other out. If you are not one of those people who play with teams well, then you better start practicing because this game forces you to do it, no matter how hard you try, you are eventually going to help your team out in one way or another. CSS also has a variety of gamemodes that can range from saving hostages and prison breaks, to defusing or planting bombs and surfing around. There are also certain servers that are more like obstacle courses than combat but nonetheless its still fun. In my opinion I find this game amazing and there is nothing bad about it that would make most people not want to play it. I have one recommendation however, add some servers that are meant for new players.

Counter-Strike: Source is a fantastic game game. If you like first person shooters, you'll love C-S:S.
Counter-Strike: Source can be a bunch of different kind of games. It's an online game and ONLINE GAME ONLY! Most of the servers on this game are usually modifications. Others are regular C-S:S servers. My favorite map would be cs_office for a regular server. Most of these modded servers are Surf, Surf RPG, Deathrun (My favorite ^^), Minigames, Prison Break, Zombie Escape/Zombie Riot, Scoutzknivez, Surf Deathmatches, Soccer and Trickz.
The 1st server I actually played on C-S:S was Steamgamers. Steamgamers (SG) is a list of modded servers in different games (including C-S:S). There are lots of people in the servers, Steam group, and forums. This link,
shows the forums to it. SG can be a game of shenanigans. Okay I'll admit, we REALLY like to do lots of shenanigans.
In the regular servers, there are 4 types of games... Defuse the bomb, Rescue the Hostages, Deathmatch and Scrim. In a game, you have to choose either Terrorist (T) or Counter-Terrorist (CT). When you're a T, you're supposed to plant the bomb in a bombing sites A or B. It usually takes about 3 seconds to plant a bomb, and the bomb goes off in 30 seconds ONCE it's placed. To plant a bomb, press your fire button (Mouse 1 recommended). A player recieves the bomb randomly, so don't expect to get a bomb every round (That is if you're the only player)!
When you're playing as a CT, you have to protect the bombing sites. When a bomb is planted, stand next to the bomb and hold E to defuse it. It will take about 15 seconds to defuse a bomb. To defuse a bomb without a long delay, you can use a defuse kit to defuse the bomb faster (You may buy this from the Equippment shop in the Buy Menu $200).
When team T fails to plant the bomb, the CT's win. And you should know by now how the T's win.
Playing Rescue the Hostages isn't difficult. The objective of the game is to, you know, rescue the hostages (This is where my fav map comes in). In order to rescue them, you need to be a CT to do this. Press E on the hostages and they will follow you, but be careful! Injuring or killing a hostage can lose you tons of money! T's may not intentionally kill the hostages. Attempting to rescue a hostage gives you $150. Saving a hostage grants you $1,000. The T's win when the CT's fail to rescue the hostages.
Deathmatch is... you know... just killing everyone (excluding your team). Each kill grants you $300. Each win is about $4,000 at a start of a round. Each loss is about $2,500. There are lots of common guns. The most common pistol is the Deagle. Deagles have 7 rounds and does high damage to the chest and -200 HP for a headshot. Each player (Not modded) has 100 HP. The most common SMG is the P90 ( 10 - 50 HP -90 - 125 HP headshot). It holds 50 rounds and has rapid fire. The 3 most common weapons are the AK47, M4A1, and Awp. Some people use the scout even though it does less damage (-50 - 99 HP, -200 - 299 HP headshot). The scout has better aim having to do with no-scoping. If you want to no-scope, I would recommend quick-switching. By quick-switching, you can either scroll your mousewheel (up then down) or Press Q twice. You can do the same with the Awp (-75 - 150 HP -350 - 460 HP headshot). But it will have a slower reaction time based on quick-switching. The most expensive gun in the game would be the M249 ($5,750) (-20 - 50 HP - 100 - 150 HP headshot). Holds 100 rounds, and is a rapid fire weapon (Slower than P90).
Now it is time to talk about our modded servers...
In Deathrun, the objective as a T is to press buttons (Using E) and activate traps to kill CT's. Some traps will require CT's to use their trickz. As a CT, you have to try and make it through every trap, but be cautious... there may be traps in the ground without buttons to push. Using your spray (Press T to spray, spray 100 times for an achievement) can help you find these traps. When you finish the map in the Deathrun map, you get to choose (some maps don't let you choose) how to kill the T(s).
Minigames is a set of random maps other people made in a mod. In SG, we mostly play Soccer maps (Or any map that has soccer in it). So it's pretty much what it is... a minigame. Every Minigames server has a different kind of minigame map. There are courses, multigames, survival, and races. The 2 races every1 plays are mg_100traps_v2 / v3 and bob1, bob2, bob3, and bob4 (Have no idea where bob came from). Usually in minigames, there is bunnyhopping (Bhop). If you want to bhop, you only need 1 command in console... bind mwheeldown +jump. To bhop, you need to time your jumps. Hyperscrolling can give you the perfect bhops. Bhopping can increase your speed as long as you strafe.
Prison break is a smart kind of C-S:S server. When you play as a T, you are prisoned (Obviously) and you have to follow the CT's orders. BUT, there's always option 2, rebelling and killing the CT's to win the round. There are LOTS of secrets in a PB map, you may find weapons in your cell. When you play as a CT, you are an officer and you MUST kill all the T's who rebel. There can be lots of kinds of rebellers. Hit & run, refusing to listen to orders, taking a Priamary Weapon, and lots of more. But if a T refuses to do an order and is NEAR the objective, you may warning shot him on the foot (Taking a secondary weapon is also a warning shot as long as the T doesn't shoot). T's may have their Last requests (LR) at the last 2 T's. There is a list of LR's you'll find out in the game.
Surfing is hard at first, but gets easier as you do it. The advice I got was imagining the ramps and using A and D to surf
(D /\ A). There are some servers that use skill timers (SG has it), so you have to surf as quick as possible.
Surf Deathmatch and RPG are the same thing, except you have to kill each other. In Surf DM, you can choose your weapons, or find them (Choosing is on SG) and surf to find various secrets. If you fall off the surf ramp, you get sent to the most common area, jail. Surf RPG is when you can use the RPG menu to upgrade stuff. You also get high XP and levels for killing people on high RPG ranks.
Playing soccer isn't hard. You just need a few commands to play soccer. Your rate has to be 25000, 30000, or 100000 (Those are the common rates) (rate 25000/30000/100000 in console). You also need your updaterate to be 66 (cl_updaterate 66). And finally, your lerp and lerp ratio has to be low. Good lerps are 0.0 - 3.0 (cl_interp 0 - 3) and your lerp ratios could be 0 - 3 (cl_interp_ratio 0 - 3). Make sure your ping is low. With these commands, you should be able to hit the ball on contact (Works for me with 0 lerp). You use your knives to hit the ball if you wanted to know.
Playing Scoutzknivez is pretty much Deathmatch with only Scout and Knife (-15 - 20 HP left click -65 HP right click -195 HP right click backstab). Usually most of the Scoutzknivez servers have low gravity, so you don't need to worry about having to try to Bunnyhop. Some servers use Roll The Dice (!rtd) to give you random buffs/debuffs. Some are also RPG, and I explained that already.
Zombie Escape is a game where you try to escape from zombies. Shooting them will knock the zombie back and will knockback far with a headshot (Strongest knockback with an awp headshot). You need to buy your equippment where you spawn. Once you get infected by a zombie, you turn into one, and once you're a zombie, you have to infect everyone else (Of course not the zombies, they're already infected!).
In Zombie Riot (Zriot) you need to kill every zombie you see. Every 5 levels a boss match will occur. And, like in ZE, you buy your weapons at spawn. When a zombie kills you once, you die and wait a short period of time to respawn. Once you die the 2nd time, you turn into a zombie. You have to then kill all the humans. (No more room, read 2/2)
A really awesome game! Really worth buying if you like fps and zombies :D

Counter-Strike: Source is a remake of Counter-Strike, and retains its team-based objective-oriented first-person shooter style gameplay. The aim of playing a map is to accomplish a map's objective: defusing the bomb, rescuing all hostages, or killing the entire opposing team. The ultimate goal of the game is to win more rounds than the opposing team. Once players are killed, they do not respawn until the next round on most servers. This gameplay feature distinguishes Counter-Strike from other first-person shooter games, where players respawn instantly or after a short delay.
Shooting while moving dramatically decreases accuracy, and holding the trigger down to continuously shoot produces severe recoil. Shot damage depends upon where the bullet hits, with hits to the head often being lethal.

There was a time, when this game was new. Graphics revealing, handling strange for the veterans. It was when a lot of people would say: "bah, you play Source? 1.6 or Condition Zero is way better, it's a classic!"
Now this game has become old itself. And I feel old, having this realization. That CS:GO is already out there, with a growing fanbase.
But why do I keep coming back to CS:Source? Every once in a while I will start this game and play a few rounds and it will make me feel good. I just think Source has extremely satisfying movements, weapon feeling and the graphics are just good enough. For a competing shooter I don't need anything else. Source keeps the perfect balance between the old, a-bit clunky feeling of 1.6 and the over-heavy, much slower and more realistic handling of CS:GO. I don't need too much realism, I don't need  bullet-spraying weapons, that don't hit, when they're supposed to!
For me, Counter Strike Source will always be the best shooter, because I grew on it. And I think there are a lot of people out there, that feel the same way. If you are below the age of 20, go for something else, otherwise this is the best dope you ever need for a quick and casual round. And there are also some nice mods out there, gungame, surfing, zombiemods, rpg, jumping, bunnyhopping maps, etc.... Man, I hope the servers will stay alive for some more years...
Now I have to call my friends and ask for a LAN, in remembrance of good ol' times

This game is the most competetive and fun shooter you are going to find for PC.the winning formula of the Source engine on this game has had an enormous effect,just like it has on every CS game.the game has no leveling system but a simple system of:the more expensive it is,the better it will perform.you kill enemies,complete objectives,win rounds.all these will give you money,you use the money to buy better weapons,if you cant afford a better weapon,than you are going to have to do with what you have.In a way,the game forces you to be a team player,but not for "the feeling".it forces you in a way thagt you will do better if you play as a team,you will get more money and you will buy better guns and equipments,its something 'bloated games'today do wrong.The gunplay is what keeps this game top notch amongs other shooters for pc.At first you are going to get killed a lot by the vets that have been playing this game for quite a while,but nothing is more satisfying that playing in a server with many other players(some even way better than you)and to manage to buy and use an AWP efficntly,or the first headshot you land with a deagle at range with perfect precision.the game will keep you on your toes at all times.a nd if you are not the type of guy who likes to stay on your toes all the time,try some custom modes.deathrun,zombies and much more will require you to sometimes outsmart your opponents and think out of the box.

There's nothing new added to it, it's just a better looking version of 1.6. Now Valve woke up and made CS: GO. Every single CS is working on the same principle: improve the graphics, hope for the best. Why add new weapons? Why change the maps? Why ADD new maps? If you are a fan of 1.6, you'll definitely love CZ, Source and GO, but if you think of the improvements Valve made for each version, you'd better through your money off the window than buy 'em. If you play CS for mini-games like Deathrun, Surf (which is not quite a mini-game) etc., then go for it. If you want just to kill people and play on regular servers, then you'd better buy CS: GO and f*ck the other versions. GG Valve, keep up the "good work"!

I don't remember why I got this game, I believe it was bundled with GMOD and CS:GO. At the time I did not have a good enough GPU to play CS:GO on anything other than the worst possible settings. I also had been playing pretty much exclusively TF2 for a couple of years. I wasn't really looking for new games, but GMOD is just kind of a must-have. One day I opened up CSS and played for a few hours on the NIGHTEAM Dust server (No, not dust 2). It was perfect. I was okay as far as aim went because of the extreme amount of time playing TF2, but the idea that you cannot be accurate when moveing was a new concept to me. I played mostly sniper in TF2 so the auto-sniper was my go-to for a while (I know, you can crucify me now). The NIGHTEAM servers all have bots that automatically join the game if there aren't enough players, so I was fighting mainly players with lots of time on the game and bots on the lowest difficulty. It was a good enough mix for me to feel like I was doing alright while still having a skill-level to shoot for. Something about the game hooked me. It definitely wasn't the graphics. It definitely wasn't the 4 different player-models. It wasn't the mass amounts of unbalanced maps, over and underpowered weapons, rampant hackers, or even the god-awful barrel physics. I think it was the community. I met so many people who were in their early 20's who played the game growing up the way I had been playing TF2. Some of them were quiet, rarely using the chat but with calling cards such as keybinds or a signature spray. Others were on the mic 24/7 swearing up a storm, but always in good fun. And some were just normal people with a good mix of the two. What all of them had in common was the amount of time they put in on that same map and server. When somebody new showed up, they weren't hard on them. When somebody new was a massive♥♥♥♥♥♥ they would be surrounded on all sides by people who would tear them apart. They never saw it coming, because they didn't know that everybody there was friends with one another. Close connections to the admins, and people who loved trash-talk in good fun, made for a very healthy server at pretty much all times. After playing as much of this game as I have, I cannot find myself playing much CS:GO without coming back to this. Something about it. Something about the game has kept itself alive. With many veteran players, new players who got the game on sale like I did, and people still hosting competitive events, it's community lives on. For now. Give it a shot!

One of my all time favorite first person shooters! It's purely a masterpiece, a work of art. If you like first person shooters than this is the game for you! Unlike Call of Duty or Battlefield the add on maps are free via the Steam workshop! If you are new to PC gaming than you should get this game before any other game. Why? Because this game rewards skill and if you don't have any (Like most new PC gamers, Including myself at the time when I was new.) it can help you build it up. Unlike CoD Counter Strike doesnt reward you for being a noob. If you get this game and you "suck" like I did when I first got it try playing by your self with bots. This game is incredibly fun to play by your self but the fun just multiplies when you add the aspect of playing with friends. If you don't have many PC gamer friends then Counter-Strike: Source is still the game for you! You can join random servers and find really cool people like your self to start playing with. If you can't decide to get Global Offensive or Source I would say go with source. Why you ask? Well Source is much easier to run but not only that it is just much more fun. Now yes this is  my personal opinion and Global Offensive vs. Source is just about like Ford vs. Chevy but if you get source you'll have the source engine which allows for many more games and free mods! Counter-Strike: Source is a 11/10 Six Star game. You will not regret this purchase!

Though deeply unsettling, Antichrist provides an incredible commentary on Psychotherapy, relationships and gender. Directed by Lars Von  Trier and starring Willem Dafoe and Charlotte Gainsbourg, this Art-House Horror film follows the story of a couple who, after their child’s death and the wife’s (Charlotte Gainsbrough) subsequent hospitalisation, retire to a cabin in the woods where the husband (Willem Dafoe) attempts to treat his wife’s grief. As the treatment continues the husband witnesses visions of a doe, a fox and a crow. Slowly the wife begins to exhibit increasingly sexually violent behaviour towards her husband and to herself, creating a cataclysmic climax and a cathartic resolution to the film. Antichrist is a difficult watch, but if you enter it with an open mind you will be treated with an incredible performance by Willem Dafoe and masterful cinematography.

Need I say best First Person Shooter out there in terms of strategy and utilising the source engine like so many before it. This is no rushing COD-esque shoot em up with whiney kids and no skill gap, but a game settled wholey on skill whether you're playing standard vanilla Search and Destroy, or one of a community servers that offers Gun Game or something like Death Run- much like Gmod with it's great players that go to the effort of setting up custom servers like these.
As for the way the game plays out, well it's physics work much like Half Life 2's does, in the way that there is restricted movement, no sprint, so there's no running from a gunfight. The balancing of the weapons is very well done, especially in terms of mid range assault rifles, clear favourites seeming to be the M4 and AK. However the way in which you purchase these said weapons at the start of each round in a game of search is you get a set amount of money based on your performance through the game. So the better you played last round, the more money you get for the next, and the more money means better guns and equipment, simple right?
Of course this game is a cult classic amongst PC gamers and it really does well for the community in how it's part of E-sports, tournaments held all over the world. This game is no pass time, Counter Strike is a way of life.

The best short description i can give of this game is that it's a hardcore team based shooter.  The long description would be an arena like firefight simulator between two factions consisting of terrorists and counter terrorists, which each have their own sets of weapons, while some weapons are universal between the two classes, there are some that are exclusive.  The other thing about the factions is that they always have opposing objectives; instead of simple TDM or CTF, this has things like bomb defusal, where the CT's attempt to find and disarm a bomb the T's have control of.  There is also a hostage rescue where the T's must guard their hostages from the rescuing CT's.  Either mode is fun but has heavy TDM overtones.
Of course the community has created and made mainstay some custom maps and gamemodes which are just as fun if not better than the actual game modes.
A word of advice however, this game is not fun for casual play, many members of it's community are seasoned veterens with hundreds if not thousands of hours in game, they know the maps the weapons and the strategies, if you do want to pick up this game, make sure you intend to get your play out if it.  Those first few matches are going to be a bit of a bloodbath on your part until you find a weapon you like and a server where you feel welcome.  But it's very well worth it if you want a shooter you can really dig in to.

This game is a classic for the FPS genre. Quite different from games like Call of Duty. If you're looking for the same Call of Duty Experience in CS:S, don't bother buying the game. They're 2 extremely different games.
On to actual gameplay, I find that it is more difficult and requires more strategy and cooperation with your teammates. There is a surplus of maps that offers a variety and taste of a different game experience each game.
There are also other gamemodes that can be entertaining if the classic 5v5 matchups don't work out for you or simply become dull. One of my favorite is the zombie mod where there is a human vs zombie type of match and the humans must try to stay alive using barricades and guns.. obviously.
Although I have only 100 hours on this game because I get an average of like 10 or 15 fps, I still come back to it sometimes to get away from the generic FPS games out there. As a classic and one of the best FPS games that have inspired many great titles today, I give it a 9/10.

Personally, Online FPS games are not something that usually attract me. I'm not the best gamer, and the thought of being competative with other serious gamers out there online, is cringe worthy. The real reason I bout CS:S was beacause Valve never let me down before, so I wasn't expecting them to do so this time.
Counter-Strike: Source is basicly what it says on the tin. A re-make of the original Counter Strike, but in the shiny new Source engine. And shiny it is. Not only just a re-skin, CS:S is a complete re-think and over-haul of the first installment, and it is done perfectly. As I said before, not a fan of Online FPS games, but as you can see I got almost a full day of gameplay out of this, so I had time to experience different game modes. The basic game mode, which is a perma-death stealth like ordeal, really didn't get anything going for me, but from the perspective of an avid FPS gamer, it is a very clever way of approaching the game and the mode itself requires alot of skill. But there are tonnes of game modes out there. Gun game, Deathmatch (my favorite) Capture the flag, as well as loads of community mods for you to try out yourself.
I was expecting to be dissapointed by this game, and I did not expect to play it as much as I did. But for me, it is a game I enjoy picking up and playing for an hour or so, leaving it and coming back, but for people who like this genre, I can see you coming back for more and more.

This game is a classic.  While many people argue over whether 1.6 is better or Global Offensive, it all boils down to a matter of opinion.  All games take place in standard Search and Destroy or Hostage Rescue format, Terrorists vs Counter-Terrorists.  You have your standard weapons, desert eagle (not the nighthawk), M4A1, AK-47, etc.
The shooting is different.  If you go in expecting Call of Duty style shooting or Battlefield, you'll be sorely disappointed.  There are no iron sights and the recoil and a lot more noticeable.  Still, after a few hours you'll get used to it.
Note, there are tons of mods to play with this game.  There's zombies, gun game, mini games and more, so give them all a try.
TL:DR - Bang bang bang.  This game is one that nearly everyone should play.  It's a different type of shooter (in terms of mechanics), but with a familiar setting.

CounterStrike: Source is, in my opinion, a massive improvement over it's predecessor, CounterStrike, known now as "CounterStrike 1.6".
The capabilities of the Source engine bring a much more immersive and content-full package than the previous instalment, and even though it was released in 2004 with visuals that are definitely taking the toll of time, it still manages to stay relevant today, still used for the hardcore tournaments we can all only dream of entering. The controls are some of the tightest ever seen in a FPS, a possession of pin-point accuracy being the only way to win. The controls seem to reach a point between the raw stages of CS:1.6, and the slightly cushioned controls of it's sequel. Matches are intense and suspenseful, with your life being your only one for the whole round with no respawns, and a pleasing array of weaponry to choose from, providing for some of the best tactical game play to be found.
The issue here is it's age however, and while the game is still relevant in tournaments, the public matches have become much less of a joy. Only the pros remain to play another day, with hackers plague servers they are not on, as less people play and report cheaters. As it stands, it's hard to find a middle ground between these two issues (if you can call the presence of good players an issue), as you constantly look for a match that is either not full of people who would legitimately♥♥♥♥♥♥you, or either full of shameless hackers who WILL illegitimately♥♥♥♥♥♥you. Furthermore, the lack of game modes has always been an issue for the early CS titles, and this one is no different, with only two official game modes available, Defuse and Hostage Rescue. Sure, other game modes have their place as mods, but these are harshly unbalanced and unpolished.
Regardless, buy this for some award winning team play and tactical game play that other franchises like Call of Duty just can't seem to provide. Essential...
+ Perfect controls
+ Exhilarating and tense tactical team game play
-  Lack of game mode options
-  Hackers... I mean difficulty.

If asked, Valve will tell you that Counter-Strike: Source originally began life as an experiment, designed to demonstrate how easy it is to port Half-Life modifications to the Source Engine. But it's easy to see how it's since established itself as Half-Life 2's chief multiplayer component; given that the majority of people who own the original Half-Life and still go online with it choose to play Counter-Strike, why waste time and resources trying to reinvent the multiplayer wheel when you can just polish an unbroken concept and re-release it as a pre-order bonus?
Go, go, go! xd
In the end, the idea turned out to be so good that Valve also decided to remake Day of Defeat, Team Fortress Classic, the original Half-Life single-player and more besides in its new Source Engine, not only attracting nostalgic fans back to retread fondly remembered paths, and gathering new blood to the shiny old flag, but saving the Seattle-based developer the trouble of designing an original multiplayer component to tack on the end of Half-Life 2 at the same time.
Having given ATI coupon holders, Condition Zero owners and LAN cafés the chance to try out a one-map beta version last month, Valve has now finally launched its Steam pre-purchase offers for Half-Life 2, and given fans who pre-order the game full access to a 'release version' of Counter-Strike: Source, featuring nine maps. Some argue that it's familiarity that fuels the success of unambitious sequels; in Valve's case, familiarity is just the kindling, and it's ignited pre-orders direct from the developer in a manner that's sure to have rival firms - including publishers - nursing furrowed brows of jealousy.
As long time veterans of the original Counter-Strike, we were some of the first in line. And having spent the past few days getting to grips with CS: Source, and reacquainting ourselves with hot headed bellowing - and, in particular, screams of "Stop running with the effing gun!" and "Defuse kit? DEFUSE KIT!" - we thought we'd let you know what you're up against; whether CS: Source is worth the trouble for fans of the original; whether it's good value as the multiplayer component of a £40 first-person shooter; and whether Valve's finally managed to give newcomers a way into the seemingly impenetrable world of Counter-Strike.
Enemy spotted
If we answered each of the last three questions in sequence, we could plot the resulting graph with a backslash. Yes, Counter-Strike: Source is "worth the trouble" for fans of the original - it's the game you remember and love, where a few minor shortfalls are offset by a resounding improvement in visual quality and a number of smaller, sensible alterations that subtly improve the experience. Secondly, maybe it's good value as the multiplayer component of a £40 FPS, but we'll deal with that in more detail later. And lastly, no, Valve's not managed to give newcomers a clearer way in.
For the completely uninitiated, CS: Source's problem is that it's too exclusive. It may be simple enough to get your head round quickly - Terrorists versus Counter-Terrorists with real-life weapons, one primary and one sidearm per player per round, bought along with grenades and suchlike before the round commences, you sit out the rest of the round when you're dead, and you can win by planting/defusing the bomb, protecting/rescuing the hostages, or killing off the other team - but it's a ♥♥♥♥♥ to master.
Valve had planned to include AI-controlled bots to help players practice their way into CS - an approach that almost worked with the much-maligned Condition Zero - but they're not in this build (something that's attracted particular criticism given that an illegal hacked version of the CS: Source beta has been circulating with the bots enabled). So, in the meantime, players are expected to pick up and learn the maps in hostile online environments, full of people (like this reviewer) who know how to kill them before they've worked out which gun to buy, or which way to turn to get from point A to point B, or even what they'll see when they do get to point B. Let alone the best map strategies, the right radio commands, the best way to handle each weapon, the best vantage points, and everything else that everybody else already knows.
Frankly, anybody coming to CS: Source afresh, hoping to pick up the multiplayer game all their friends rave about, is going to have their work just as cut out as ever, and may prefer to wait for Valve to activate the bots so they can practice and grasp the fundamentals - how the game works, which weapons to go for and why, the map layouts, and the best team strategies - offline, before heading online to start nailing down the subtleties, like the way crouching improves firing accuracy, how you move quicker with the knife drawn than a primary weapon, and what to expect from individual chokepoints in a live game.
Need backup
For existing fans though, CS: Source ought to provide ideal fodder on those increasingly cold winter nights. In gameplay terms it's almost indistinguishable from its Half-Life-based predecessor. Two teams race towards chokepoints and try to achieve their objectives against the clock, taking advantage of the wide variety of weapons and tactics at their disposal, and the departed troops get to sit around and spectate as they do so, chatting about the action and sharing in the pervading mood of the encounter. It makes you laugh (particularly when it's one v. one and someone accidentally kills himself with a grenade or falling damage), and it makes you cry (particularly when people run with their bloody guns), but, given time to prove itself, it's also one of the most arresting FPS disciplines in existence.
Or, to make that a bit clearer, in gameplay terms the only practical differences can be run through in a couple of paragraphs. You can smash crates, computers and plenty of other destructible items littering each level. Glass, when hit by a bullet or knife, only falls away in a small radius around the point of impact, so it now takes another bullet or somebody jumping through the frosted effect of the cracked remnants to make it through completely. You can no longer penetrate two-foot walls with bullets, and a grenade going off on the other side of a wall will no longer hurt you anywhere near as much, but you can still send bullets through boxes, cupboard doors and the like. Water now splashes visually as well as audibly, giving the defending side on maps like Aztec a bit of an advantage in locating intrepid aggressors. And hostages are now capable of following you without getting stuck every five seconds, even if they still do so every once in a while.
And, of course, CS: Source adopts Half-Life 2's Havok-based physics code, meaning that barrels and limp bodies are now thrown around semi-convincingly by explosions (although they do seem to bounce a bit too much at the moment), adding to the spectacle. The gameplay benefits of this are, in practice, almost negligible (you'll be lucky to benefit from any extra cover as a result of it, in any case), but it certainly contributes to the increased believability of the whole thing.
7/10

Unarguably one of my favorite PC games of all times, Counter-Strike: Source is a MUST-PLAY for every PC gamer! Having been played for over 5 years by many, casual and competitive players alike, it's no surprise that this game holds up to this date, and since this mod was made by Valve, makes this ever more of a unique, fun and somewhat balanced experience.
This game's straight-forward, teamplay-strategy gameplay is what sets CS:S apart from "Call Of Duty-esque" games we see on the market nowadays: it offers intensity to the matches, making each round feel fresh and new. The gunplay is also different, but balanced: no gun is ever the same (obviously), and the in-game money you earn from kills and completing objectives  will make you decide between an expensive AWP and a helpful Kevlar vest.
That, and the fact, that this game's mod-friendly increases the replay value considerably, makes you wanting for more Counter-Strike, even after a long hiatus.
